title: Security is a form of care
excerpt: Moving beyond fear-driven security toward systems that respect attention, dignity, and ordinary human behavior.

sections.label: Argument
sections.title: Security should make safe behavior easier.
paragraphs: People are often described as the weakest link. That phrase hides design failures. If the secure path demands constant vigilance, memorization, and interruption, the system has delegated its complexity to the person least equipped to resolve it.

sections.label: Design
sections.title: Build calm defaults.
points: Explain consequences in specific, familiar language
Measure interruption and confusion as security costs

sections.label: Closing
sections.title: Protection without dignity is incomplete.
paragraphs: Good security respects people’s time and context. It quietly creates room for them to do meaningful work without needing to become security experts first.
